actual_scope: For the pinned helper-462 matcher, the rational elementary alphabet of shears, single-coordinate scales and axis swaps contains a zero-swap word with exactly one scale. The exhibited word has 53 dyadic shears and one final scale by -16. Under the additional hypothesis that every shear coefficient is an integer, no zero-swap one-scale word exists. No supplier admission, tariff comparison, or new kappa.
scope_change_reason: Handoff comment 19137812 asks for one literal N-dimensional stock/owner/route generator. Finding 19492596 and fork draft PR 150 already give a 0-swap, 7-scale, 27-shear word and the determinant lower bound of one scale. This package answers only the remaining one-scale existence question for that pinned matcher. It does not audit #5717/#5719, price inherited P2 tariffs, or search for fewer than 27 shears at two or more scales.
bottleneck_link: The route ledger is one charged part of the missing physical generator. One scale is necessary by the determinant identity and sufficient in the rational alphabet, so a later generator cannot treat seven scales as forced. The integer-coefficient obstruction says that sufficiency uses a genuine dyadic shear. Shear length and the interchange/shear tariff remain open, so this is not a supplier admission.
stop_rule: Stop after the explicit one-scale word, the determinant identity, the integer-coefficient obstruction, the minor census, and the failure controls. Do not shorten the shear count, price P2 tariffs, or build the N-dimensional compiler.
evidence: Exact rational product of the frozen 0-swap, 1-scale, 53-shear word equals the pinned matcher. The same elimination works with the scale on every row. Rank 5 over F2 makes every 6x6 minor even, while every one-coordinate integer scale by -16 has a 6x6 identity minor, so no integer-shear zero-swap one-scale word exists. The exhaustive minor census gives determinantal divisors (1,1,1,1,1,2,4,16).

open_questions.question: What is the minimal number of shears in a zero-swap word that uses exactly one scale?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The elimination in this package has 53 shears on every coordinate. That length is an upper bound. It sits above the known 7-scale schedule of 27 shears, so it does not improve the shear count.
open_questions.first_step: Keep exactly one scale of coefficient -16 and replace one balanced-scale block by a shorter shear identity, then recheck the product against the pinned matcher.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package stops at existence. A shorter explicit word would still be an upper bound unless the search is exhaustive.

open_questions.question: Is there a zero-swap word for this matcher with at least two scales and fewer than 27 shears?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The published swap-free schedule uses 7 scales and 27 shears. The one-scale witness uses 53 shears. Neither answers the two-or-more-scale shortening question.
open_questions.first_step: Search words whose scale coefficients multiply to -16, with scale count at least 2 and shear count at most 26.
open_questions.blocked_by: That search is a separate question. This package does not run it.

open_questions.question: With the inherited P2 tariffs, does any legal word beat the published pair on the completed ordinary bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Letter counts do not determine the signed moment. Removing swaps and adding shears can move the bill in either direction.
open_questions.first_step: Pin the inherited ordered-affine, unit-scaling and completed-interchange costs used by research/bit-completed-backend-api and evaluate one legal word at that invocation.
open_questions.blocked_by: Those primitive tariffs are a separate comparison. This package records no bill.
